ground_truth_core_content:
Introduction:
**1:** The generated section covers the closed-book exam framing, hallucination risk, fine-tuning limitations (resource-heavy, dataset curation, multi-day training, catastrophic forgetting), and context-window limitations (cost, latency, lost-in-the-middle) with the same substance as the expected section. The brief "advanced and agentic patterns" preview mirrors the expected section's own preview at a reduced level of detail; per the standing ruling, this reduced detail is not penalized since the essential idea is still present (unlike a prior replicate where the agentic angle was omitted entirely). The Lesson-10 memory contrast and RAG-as-open-book-exam solution are both present and substantively equivalent.

The RAG System: Core Components:
**1:** Both sections cover the same three pillars — Retrieval, Augmentation, and Generation — with matching substance. The generated section's added ChatGPT-lawyer hallucination anecdote and HNSW/LSH indexing detail are additions rather than omissions and don't affect the core ideas, which are otherwise complete.

The RAG Pipeline: Ingestion and Retrieval:
**0:** Both sections cover the same two-phase structure with matching substance, and both reference Lesson 4's structured outputs. The generated section's LangChain-vs-LlamaIndex code comparison is a valid addition, not an omission. However, as in every replicate of this lesson graded so far, two ideas present in the expected section are absent: (1) the callout on long-context/asymmetric-search embedding models; (2) the guidance on tuning chunk size empirically against retrieval metrics (hit rate/recall, MRR@k, nDCG@k) and the specific chunk-size/overlap ranges. These remain substantive, non-trivial ideas in the expected section with no equivalent here.

Advanced RAG Techniques:
**1:** Both sections cover the same six techniques — Hybrid Search, Re-ranking, Query Transformations, Advanced Chunking, GraphRAG, and Metadata Filtering — with matching substance. The generated section's added statistics (NVIDIA's 9% recall-gap benchmark, the Stanford 35–45% GraphRAG finding, Anthropic's 49% Contextual Retrieval figure) and the added LlamaIndex auto-routing code example are additions rather than omissions and don't affect the core ideas, which are otherwise complete.

Agentic RAG:
**1:** Both sections cover the standard-vs-agentic distinction, the ReAct-loop tie-in, and all four agentic capabilities — iterative refinement, dynamic source selection, information fusion, and the knowledge-base-update capability correctly previewed toward Lesson 10 — plus the same Thought/Action/Observation worked example.

Conclusion:
**1:** Both sections cover the same key takeaways: RAG as the primary industry solution to the LLM knowledge problem, the necessity of advanced techniques for production quality, the agentic future of retrieval, the three core benefits, RAG's status as a foundational competency and subset of Context Engineering, and the same transition preview into Lesson 10 plus future topics.
